title: Usage Insights Analytics API Contract (Draft) — route/model cost drivers + exports
content:
LAST UPDATED: 2026-02-19
DOC OWNER: Jada Williams
STATUS: Draft for internal review (Console + Telemetry + Security)

Purpose
- Define the HTTP API contract powering the Console “Usage Insights” experience:
  - Top routes list (ranked by spend)
  - Route detail (model breakdown + change vs prior period)
  - Exports (CSV + JSON) suitable for FinOps / incident reviews
- This is a contract draft (wire-level). Backing datasets/rollups and exact metric derivations are tracked separately.

Non-goals (contract scope)
- No customer-defined arbitrary dimensions (beyond route + model + standard filters).
- No anomaly detection endpoints.
- No scheduled exports in v1.

Audience
- Console backend + frontend
- Telemetry/analytics pipeline
- SRE (SLOs, caching, query budgets)
- Security/compliance (RBAC, audit logging)

============================================================
1) API overview
============================================================
Base URL
- Production: https://api.redwoodinference.com
- Staging: https://api.staging.redwoodinference.com

API namespace
- /v1/usage-insights/...

Auth
- Same as Redwood API: Bearer token (org-scoped), plus project scoping via headers or token claims.
- All endpoints MUST enforce org_id + project_id boundaries. No cross-project aggregation.

Required headers
- Authorization: Bearer <token>
- X-Redwood-Org-Id: <org_id>
- X-Redwood-Project-Id: <project_id>

Optional headers
- X-Redwood-Request-Id: <client request id> (echoed back)

Idempotency
- Export job creation supports Idempotency-Key to avoid duplicate jobs.

Rate limits (initial proposal; subject to tuning)
- GET routes list: 60 rpm per project
- GET route detail: 120 rpm per project
- POST export job: 10 rpm per project
- GET export job status/download: 60 rpm per project

Freshness + late-arriving metering events
- Endpoints return aggregates that are near-real-time but may be revised as late events arrive.
- We will expose a “data_freshness” object in responses (timestamps + lag hints) to help explain invoice mismatches.

Time window semantics
- All query windows are [start, end) (inclusive of start, exclusive of end)
- Times are ISO-8601 UTC timestamps.
- Maximum range differs by endpoint (see limits).

Granularity
- Top routes endpoint returns one row per route for the queried window (no time series in v1).
- Route detail endpoint can optionally return a time series (hourly/daily) for sparklines and “what changed” UX.

============================================================
2) Core concepts + definitions
============================================================
Route
- route is a customer-supplied or gateway-derived identifier representing an application endpoint or logical feature.
- Contract uses two route fields:
  - route: the normalized route string (human-readable; may be “unknown”)
  - route_key: stable identifier used for lookups (hashed/encoded when route is too long or disallowed)

Normalization (summary)
- Enforced upstream per ADR “route dimension definition and normalization”. This API assumes data is already normalized.
- API will still guard against unsafe characters on input where route is passed.

Model
- model is the “served model identifier” at time of inference, e.g. "llama-3.1-70b-instruct" or "qwen2.5-32b".
- For fallback/routing: attribution is by route always; model breakdown reflects the actual served model(s).

Cost fields
- cost_usd: attributable cost for the window (post-metering), in USD.
- unit_cost_usd_per_1k_output_tokens: derived estimate. Intended for ranking/intuition, not billing.

Token fields
- input_tokens, output_tokens
- cached_input_tokens, cached_output_tokens (tokens that hit cache and were billed differently or not billed)

Performance fields
- latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms (end-to-end request latency)
- error_rate: errors / total requests, where error is non-2xx or internal error class mapping

============================================================
3) Common query parameters
============================================================
Common filters (where applicable)
- start: ISO-8601 UTC
- end: ISO-8601 UTC
- environment: one of ["prod", "staging", "dev"] (optional)
- region: cloud region code, e.g. "us-east-1" (optional)
- deployment_mode: ["hosted", "dedicated", "private"] (optional)
- route_prefix: string (optional; prefix match on normalized route)
- model: string (optional; filter to a model)

Pagination
- We use cursor-based pagination:
  - limit: integer (default 50, max 200)
  - cursor: opaque string from prior response

Sorting
- sort: enum
  - cost_desc (default)
  - cost_asc
  - latency_p95_desc
  - error_rate_desc
  - requests_desc

Limits (proposal)
- GET /routes max time range: 31 days
- GET /routes/{route_key} max time range for time series: 31 days
- Export max time range: 90 days (subject to size cap)

============================================================
4) Endpoint: List routes (top drivers)
============================================================
GET /v1/usage-insights/routes

Description
- Returns routes ranked by total cost for a given time window, with key cost + perf metrics.
- Designed for the Console “Routes” table.

Query params
- start (required)
- end (required)
- limit (optional)
- cursor (optional)
- sort (optional)
- environment, region, deployment_mode (optional)
- model (optional)
- route_prefix (optional)
- include_unknown_route: boolean (optional; default true)

Response 200 (example)
{
  "request_id": "b3f1d7b5-7d3f-4e33-9a1d-3f3dc12e5f4e",
  "start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-08T00:00:00Z",
  "filters": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted",
    "model": null,
    "route_prefix": null,
    "include_unknown_route": true
  },
  "data_freshness": {
    "as_of": "2026-02-08T00:10:00Z",
    "estimated_lag_seconds": 420,
    "notes": "Aggregates may update for late-arriving metering events."
  },
  "page": {
    "limit": 50,
    "cursor": null,
    "next_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjUwfQ=="
  },
  "routes": [
    {
      "route_key": "rt_2f1a7c7b7c",
      "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
      "requests": 183204,
      "cost_usd": 12984.12,
      "input_tokens": 98231422,
      "output_tokens": 52123310,
      "cached_input_tokens": 12003411,
      "cached_output_tokens": 0,
      "unit_cost_usd_per_1k_output_tokens": 0.249,
      "latency_p50_ms": 410,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1320,
      "error_rate": 0.0032
    },
    {
      "route_key": "rt_8b19bd6a10",
      "route": "/v1/embeddings",
      "requests": 812300,
      "cost_usd": 8442.77,
      "input_tokens": 220991003,
      "output_tokens": 0,
      "cached_input_tokens": 44122011,
      "cached_output_tokens": 0,
      "unit_cost_usd_per_1k_output_tokens": null,
      "latency_p50_ms": 55,
      "latency_p95_ms": 120,
      "error_rate": 0.0004
    }
  ]
}

Notes
- unit_cost_usd_per_1k_output_tokens is null for endpoints with output_tokens == 0 (embeddings/rerank).
- cost_usd is aggregate attribution, not invoice total; customers may see mismatch due to:
  - invoice includes other fees
  - export window alignment
  - late-arriving events
  - retention/backfill behavior

Error responses
- 400 invalid_time_range: end <= start OR exceeds max window
- 401 unauthorized
- 403 forbidden (RBAC / project boundary)
- 429 rate_limited

============================================================
5) Endpoint: Route detail (overview + model breakdown + deltas)
============================================================
GET /v1/usage-insights/routes/{route_key}

Description
- Returns aggregate metrics for a single route over a window.
- Optionally includes:
  - breakdown_by_model
  - compare_to (prior period) deltas
  - time_series for sparklines

Path params
- route_key (required)

Query params
- start (required)
- end (required)
- environment, region, deployment_mode (optional)
- include_model_breakdown: boolean (optional; default true)
- include_time_series: boolean (optional; default false)
- time_series_granularity: ["hour", "day"] (optional; required if include_time_series)
- compare_to: ["none", "previous_period"] (optional; default "previous_period")
- model: string (optional; if specified, returns route metrics filtered to the model and omits breakdown)

Response 200 (example)
{
  "request_id": "bbef41c0-27e8-4c7a-a7f2-4f0b83d9c0b1",
  "route_key": "rt_2f1a7c7b7c",
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-08T00:00:00Z",
  "filters": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted",
    "model": null
  },
  "data_freshness": {
    "as_of": "2026-02-08T00:10:00Z",
    "estimated_lag_seconds": 420
  },
  "totals": {
    "requests": 183204,
    "cost_usd": 12984.12,
    "input_tokens": 98231422,
    "output_tokens": 52123310,
    "cached_input_tokens": 12003411,
    "cached_output_tokens": 0,
    "latency_p50_ms": 410,
    "latency_p95_ms": 1320,
    "error_rate": 0.0032
  },
  "compare_to": {
    "mode": "previous_period",
    "baseline_start": "2026-01-25T00:00:00Z",
    "baseline_end": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
    "deltas": {
      "cost_usd": 1821.55,
      "cost_usd_pct": 0.163,
      "requests": 14402,
      "requests_pct": 0.085,
      "latency_p95_ms": 110,
      "latency_p95_ms_pct": 0.091,
      "error_rate": 0.0006,
      "error_rate_pct": 0.230
    },
    "notes": "Percent deltas are (current-baseline)/baseline. If baseline is 0, pct is null."
  },
  "model_breakdown": [
    {
      "model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
      "requests": 120004,
      "cost_usd": 9488.23,
      "input_tokens": 65122001,
      "output_tokens": 39011220,
      "cached_input_tokens": 8011020,
      "cached_output_tokens": 0,
      "latency_p50_ms": 430,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1405,
      "error_rate": 0.0038
    },
    {
      "model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct-awq",
      "requests": 63200,
      "cost_usd": 3495.89,
      "input_tokens": 33109421,
      "output_tokens": 13112090,
      "cached_input_tokens": 3992391,
      "cached_output_tokens": 0,
      "latency_p50_ms": 360,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1180,
      "error_rate": 0.0021
    }
  ],
  "time_series": [
    {
      "bucket_start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
      "bucket_end": "2026-02-02T00:00:00Z",
      "cost_usd": 1710.33,
      "requests": 24210,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1290,
      "error_rate": 0.0031
    },
    {
      "bucket_start": "2026-02-02T00:00:00Z",
      "bucket_end": "2026-02-03T00:00:00Z",
      "cost_usd": 1842.10,
      "requests": 26102,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1340,
      "error_rate": 0.0034
    }
  ]
}

Notes
- When model query param is provided, model_breakdown is omitted and totals reflect only that model.
- If include_time_series=false, time_series is omitted.

Errors
- 404 route_not_found (route_key not present for project, or filtered away by RBAC)

============================================================
6) Endpoint: Model breakdown (standalone; optional)
============================================================
NOTE: We may not need this if route detail always includes model_breakdown. Keeping here as an alternative contract to reduce payload size.

GET /v1/usage-insights/routes/{route_key}/models

Query params
- start, end (required)
- environment, region, deployment_mode (optional)
- limit (optional; default 20, max 100)  // number of models

Response 200 (example)
{
  "request_id": "a4d403c7-cc07-4c2f-9d23-4b8c67b7c64a",
  "route_key": "rt_2f1a7c7b7c",
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-08T00:00:00Z",
  "models": [
    {
      "model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct",
      "cost_usd": 9488.23,
      "requests": 120004,
      "latency_p95_ms": 1405,
      "error_rate": 0.0038
    }
  ]
}

============================================================
7) Export jobs
============================================================
Design goals
- Exports are asynchronous (job-based) to avoid tying up API workers.
- Export must be auditable (create + download events) and RBAC-protected.
- Exports must be bounded (time range + max rows + file size).

7.1 Create export job
POST /v1/usage-insights/exports

Headers
- Idempotency-Key: <uuid> (recommended)

Request body (example)
{
  "start": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-02-08T00:00:00Z",
  "filters": {
    "environment": "prod",
    "region": "us-east-1",
    "deployment_mode": "hosted",
    "route_prefix": null,
    "model": null
  },
  "dimensions": ["route", "model"],
  "metrics": [
    "cost_usd",
    "requests",
    "input_tokens",
    "output_tokens",
    "cached_input_tokens",
    "cached_output_tokens",
    "latency_p50_ms",
    "latency_p95_ms",
    "error_rate"
  ],
  "format": "csv",
  "max_rows": 200000,
  "time_series_granularity": "day"
}

Request field notes
- dimensions allowed sets (v1):
  - ["route"]
  - ["route","model"]
- If time_series_granularity is provided, export includes a time bucket column; otherwise totals-only per dimension.
- max_rows is a hard stop; job fails with export_too_large if estimated rows exceed.

Response 201 (example)
{
  "request_id": "c8d1d44a-7b27-4d8b-8b94-bd4f1f930f19",
  "export_id": "exp_01HRM7TZD3TQ6N8PZB7P1AJ6R3",
  "status": "queued",
  "created_at": "2026-02-08T00:12:03Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-02-15T00:12:03Z",
  "format": "csv",
  "download": {
    "url": null,
    "available": false
  }
}

Export job audit logging (implementation requirement)
- Creating an export job MUST emit an audit event including:
  - actor_id / actor_email
  - org_id / project_id
  - time window start/end
  - filters + dimensions + metrics
  - export_id

7.2 Get export job status
GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}

Response 200 (example)
{
  "request_id": "d3e7a7c1-9d9b-46bc-9a8f-8c4b238b2f8a",
  "export_id": "exp_01HRM7TZD3TQ6N8PZB7P1AJ6R3",
  "status": "complete",
  "created_at": "2026-02-08T00:12:03Z",
  "started_at": "2026-02-08T00:12:08Z",
  "completed_at": "2026-02-08T00:12:40Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-02-15T00:12:03Z",
  "format": "csv",
  "row_count": 48210,
  "byte_count": 9183310,
  "sha256": "b2d12a6f...",
  "download": {
    "available": true,
    "url": "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/usage-insights/exports/exp_01HRM7TZD3TQ6N8PZB7P1AJ6R3/download"
  },
  "failure": null
}

Failure example
{
  "export_id": "exp_...",
  "status": "failed",
  "failure": {
    "code": "export_too_large",
    "message": "Estimated rows exceed max_rows. Reduce time range or dimensions.",
    "details": "estimated_rows=912340 max_rows=200000"
  }
}

7.3 Download export
GET /v1/usage-insights/exports/{export_id}/download

Behavior
- Returns 302 to a signed object store URL OR streams bytes directly (TBD). We must support large files; prefer signed URL.
- Download MUST emit an audit event:
  - actor_id / actor_email
  - export_id
  - timestamp
  - client_ip (if available)
  - user_agent (if available)

CSV schema (proposed; subject to schema-versioning policy)
- Columns (totals-only):
  - org_id, project_id, environment, region, deployment_mode
  - start, end
  - route_key, route
  - model (if requested)
  - cost_usd, requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cached_output_tokens
  - latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, error_rate
  - data_as_of

If time_series_granularity provided:
- Adds: bucket_start, bucket_end

Schema versioning
- Response headers on download:
  - X-Redwood-Export-Schema-Version: 1
- Any column additions must be additive; removals require a new schema version.

============================================================
8) Error model (consistent across endpoints)
============================================================
All non-2xx return
{
  "request_id": "...",
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_time_range",
    "message": "end must be after start",
    "details": "start=... end=..."
  }
}

Proposed error codes
- invalid_time_range
- invalid_filter
- invalid_cursor
- route_not_found
- export_not_found
- export_not_ready
- export_expired
- export_too_large
- query_budget_exceeded
- unauthorized
- forbidden
- rate_limited
- internal

============================================================
9) Performance + caching notes
============================================================
Server-side caching
- Top routes endpoint should be cacheable by (org_id, project_id, start, end, filters, sort, cursor) for a short TTL (e.g., 30–60s) to protect the warehouse.
- Route detail similarly cacheable; note that late-arriving events can invalidate totals. Our current stance: short TTL is acceptable; data_freshness exposes staleness.

Query cost budgets
- Console needs predictable p95. If query_budget_exceeded, return 503 with code query_budget_exceeded (or 429?) and a retry-after.

============================================================
10) Open questions (need review)
============================================================
1) Do we want a standalone /routes/{route_key}/models endpoint, or keep model_breakdown exclusively on route detail?
2) Should /routes include a “top_models” preview column (e.g., top 3 models by cost) for the table?
3) For route_key vs route in route detail lookup: do we allow GET by route string? (Security + normalization risks; leaning NO.)
4) Exports: signed URL redirect vs streaming. Signed URL preferred; confirm compliance stance.
5) Should we expose “billable_tokens” vs raw tokens? Finance is likely to ask.

============================================================
11) Change log
============================================================
2026-02-19
- Added data_freshness object to list and detail responses.
- Clarified export schema version header.
- Added compare_to delta fields.

2026-02-03
- Initial draft covering routes list, route detail, export job create/status/download.
